main_body: Round stone well: a light grey stone rim ring around a dark-blue water opening, with a block-stone front face below. A wooden roof beam and posts sit above it.
top_band: Light grey-green rim at rows ~14-17, enclosing a dark blue water ellipse at rows ~17-21, ending in a front rim at ~21-22
evidence: Down the middle column, the roof and pulley come first. Then the light stone back rim (rows ~14-16) and the dark blue water ellipse with a highlight (rows ~17-21) follow. A lighter front rim edge comes next, then the darker block-stone front face (rows ~23-31) with a shaded course. The opening is a real elliptical interior with several rows of height, so the horizontal surface reads clearly from above. There is no receding side face.

style.evidence: The stone has about 5 steps, with a light rim, mid and dark blocks, a deep base and blue water. The outlines are dark tinted tones rather than black. The wooden roof beam is a large flat orange slab (about 30x4 px) with only a highlight line and a dark underside. It has no grain or planks, unlike the roofed reference's tiled, textured roof. The posts are flat single-tone columns. The stone blocks are fairly large smooth fills with little speckle. Overall it is thinner and flatter than the Beodeul well.
